rows.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، ابن زيد
rows.claim: They identify those indicated as the prophets previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: أي الانبياء المذكورين كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والسدي وأبن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: An alternative identifies them as the believers entrusted with duties; al-Alusi says this view is untenable.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الاشارة إلى المؤمنين الموكلين وروي ذلك عن الحسن وقتادة ولا يخفى ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the prophets to truth and the straight path; naming God explicitly signals that He is the cause of their guidance, while the destination is clear.
rows.anchor: أي هديناهم إلى الحق والصراط المستقيم والالتفات إلى الاسم الجليل للاشعار بعلة الهداية وحفظ المهدي اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command restricts emulation to their guidance collectively: faith in God, His oneness, and the fundamentals of religion.
rows.anchor: اجعل هداهم منفردا بالاقتداء واجعل الاقتداء مقصورا عليه والمراد بهداهم عند جمع طريقهم في الايمان بالله تعالى وتوحيده وأصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their abrogated laws are excluded because they cease to be guidance after abrogation and the prophets differed over them, so they cannot all be imitated.
rows.anchor: دون الشرائع القابلة للنسخ فانها بعد النسخ لا تبقى هدى وهم أيضا مختلفون فيها فلا يمكن التأسي بهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following them means taking the path because it accords with reason and revelation, which honors the prophets as adherents of the truth.
rows.anchor: بل من حيث أنه طريق العقل والشرع ففي ذلك تعظيم لهم على أن طريقهم هو الحق الموافق لدليل العقل والسمع

rows.speaker: العلامة الثاني
rows.claim: He answers that the Prophet follows the prophets' guidance because it is the rational and revealed truth, not by imitating their beliefs.
rows.anchor: وبهذا أجاب العلامة الثاني عما أورده سؤالا من أن الواجب في الاعتقادات وأصول الدين هو اتباع الدليل من العقل والسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that if the Prophet's belief rests on proof rather than their belief, the command to follow their guidance has no purpose.
rows.anchor: وأورد عليه أن اعتقاده عليه الصلاة والسلام حينئذ ليس لأجل اعتقادهم بل لأجل الدليل فلا معنى لامره بالاقتداء بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another objection notes that the Prophet had already adopted the fundamentals before this verse; the command might therefore mean to remain steadfast in them.
rows.anchor: واعترض أيضا بأن الأخذ باصول الدين حاصل له قبل نزول اة ية فلا معنى للامر بأخذ ما قد أخذ قبل اللهم الا أن يحمل

rows.speaker: القطب الرازي
rows.claim: He holds that the command concerns virtuous character and perfect qualities, such as forbearance, patience, asceticism, gratitude, and humility.
rows.anchor: وحقق القطب الرازي في حواشيه على الكشاف أنه يتعين ان الاقتداء المأمور به ليس إلا في الاخلاق الفاضلة والصفات الكاملة كالحلم والصبر

rows.speaker: القطب الرازي
rows.claim: The verse proves Muhammad superior to every prophet: infallibility entails that he fulfilled all their virtues, gathering in himself the qualities distributed among them.
rows.anchor: إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قد أمتثل وآتى بجميع ذلك وصل تلك الاخلاق الفاضلة التي في جميعهم فاجتمع فيه من خصال الكمال ما كان متفرقا فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final hāʾ in اقتده is a pause marker, retained even in connected recitation by analogy with pause; Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAsim read it this way.
rows.anchor: هاء السكت التي تزاد في الوقف ساكنة أيضا اجراء للوصل مجرى الوقف وبذلك قرا ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They omit the pause hāʾ specifically in connected recitation.
rows.anchor: ويحذف الهاء في الوصل خاصة حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads the hāʾ with an unlengthened kasra; Hisham transmits this, while other transmitters lengthen it with a following yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ( اقتده ) بكسر الهاء من غير اشباع وهو الذي تسميه القراء

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Mujahid calls Ibn ʿAmir's reading erroneous because a pause hāʾ should never be vocalized.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو بكر بن مجاهد أن قراءة ابن عامر غلط معللا ذلك بان الهاء هاء الوقف

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi counters that the hāʾ is a pronoun for the verbal noun, meaning اقتد الاقتداء, rather than a pause marker.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه أبو علي الفارسي بأن الهاء ضمير المصدر وليست هاء السكت

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa cites a poetic example where hāʾ is the pronoun for درس, not an object, since يدرس already takes القرآن as its object.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو البقاء قوله : هذا سراقة للقرآن يدرسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some allow a pause hāʾ to take a vowel by analogy with a pronoun, since Arabic often gives one form the ruling of a similar form.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن هاء السكت قد تحرك تشبيها لها بهاء الضمير

rows.speaker: أبو الطيب
rows.claim: A poetic line is cited as a pause hāʾ reportedly read with either ḍamma or kasra by analogy with a pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقد روي قول أبي الطيب :

rows.speaker: صاحب الدر المصون
rows.claim: He prefers explaining the kasra as resolving two adjacent sukūns, since a pronoun hāʾ is not kasra after an alif.
rows.anchor: واستحسن صاحب الدر المصون جعل الكسر لالتقاء الساكنين لا لشبه الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that the connected hāʾ was added to follow the codex exemplar, since that would make untransmitted recitation follow script alone.
rows.anchor: ورعم الامام أن اثبات الهاء في الوصل للاقتداء بالامام ولا يقتدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no payment for the Quran or its delivery, as the context indicates, just as earlier prophets asked none from their peoples.
rows.anchor: أي لا أطلب منكم ( عليه ( أي على القرآن أو على التبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qutb's account treats refusing payment for beneficence as part of the prophets' exemplary moral guidance; others see tension with restricting guidance to fundamentals.
rows.anchor: وهذا من جملة ما أمرنا بالاقتداء به من هداهم عليهم السلام وهو ظاهر على ما قاله القطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If guidance is limited to fundamentals, the refusal of payment can still be a separate commanded example; fronting the object denies following another way in this matter.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن استفادة الاقتداء بالأصول من الأمر الأول لا ينافي أن يؤمر عليه الصلاة والسلام بالاقتداء بأمر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is used as evidence that payment may be taken for teaching and conveying religious rulings, a matter discussed extensively by jurists.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على أنه يحل أخذ الأجر للتعليم وتبليغ الأحكام وفيه كلام للفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that Muhammad was bound by the law of earlier prophets, but al-Alusi rejects this inference.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بها على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم متعبد بشرع من قبله وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to follow the prophets' guidance rather than merely imitate the prophets themselves hints to spiritually perceptive readers at Muhammad's exalted rank.
rows.anchor: وفي أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام بالاقتداء بهم دون الاقتداء بهم ما لا يخفى من الاشارة إلى علو مقامه صلى الله عليه وسلم عند أرباب الذوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in إن هو refers to the Quran; dhikrā means reminder, a verbal noun attached to the Quran pronoun for emphasis without needing to recast it as a noun meaning reminder.
rows.anchor: أي ما القرآن ( إلا ذكرى ( أي تذكير فهو مصدر وحمله على ضمير القرآن للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is for all peoples, so the Prophet's mission is universal and not limited to any one community.
rows.anchor: كافة فلا يختص به قوم دون ءاخرين واستدل باة ية على عموم بعثته

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reports that polytheists asked why animals killed by God were forbidden while those killed by people, a falcon, or a dog were lawful; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: فقد ذكر الواحدي أن المشركين قالوا : يا محمد أخبرنا عن الشاة إذا ماتت من قتلها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Persian Magians wrote Quraysh after carrion was forbidden, arguing that Muhammad's followers allowed what they slaughtered but forbade what God killed; some Muslims were troubled and the verse came down.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة : إن المجوس من أهل فارس لما أنزل الله تعالى تحريم الميتة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews asked the Prophet whether they could eat what they killed but not what God killed; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : جاءت اليهود إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means eating animals slaughtered with God's name, not those dedicated to another alongside or instead of Him, and not carrion; the restriction follows from the prior warning and conditional wording.
rows.anchor: كلوا مما ذكر اسم الله تعالى على ذبحه لا مما ذكر عليه أسم غيره خاصة أو مع اسمه عز اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some deny that the verse itself restricts the permission, arguing that the explicit prohibition of food without God's name appears in 6:121; al-Alusi says this opposes the majority.
rows.anchor: أعني قوله تعالى : ( ولا تأكلوا مما ) الخ وهو مخالف لما عليه الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God's signs, including the rulings on this issue, entails allowing what God permits and avoiding what He prohibits.
rows.anchor: فان الايمان بها يقتضي استباحة ما أحل الله تعالى واجتناب ما حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative readings of the conditional mean either knowing the realities through faith or being firmly convinced, since faith can be imitative, conjectural, or verified.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ان صرتم عالمين حقائق الأمور التي هذا الأمر من جملتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase is attached to what follows and fronted to preserve the rhyme; the conditional answer is omitted because the preceding clause supplies it.
rows.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بما بعده وقدم رعاية للفواصل وجواب الشرط محذوف لدلالة ما قبله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns animals and appears to cover omitted invocation whether deliberate or forgetful; Dawud, Ahmad, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, and al-Jubba'i hold that view.
rows.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في تحريم متروك التسمية عمدا كان أو نسيانا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits slaughter without the invocation, citing a mursal report from Rashid ibn Saʿd that a Muslim's slaughter is lawful whether God's name was mentioned or not.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي بخلافه لما لما رواه أبو داود وعبد بن حميد عن راشد بن سعد مرسلا

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The relied-upon Maliki position forbids intentionally omitted invocation, whether the omission reflects negligence or another reason; Ashhab has an anomalous permissive view for non-negligent omission.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك وهي الرواية المعولعليها عند أئمة مذهبه ان متروك التسمية عمدا لا يؤكل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa distinguishes deliberate omission from forgetfulness, as does the sound Maliki position; the later claim that Malik agrees with al-Shafiʿi or Dawud conflicts with Maliki books.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الامام أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه التفرقة بين العمد والنسيان كالصحيح من مذهب مالك

rows.speaker: العلامة الثاني
rows.claim: Al-ʿAllama al-Thani argues that forgetful omission is not true omission because the invocation remains in the Muslim's heart, citing the Prophetic answer to eat it.
rows.anchor: قال العلامة الثاني : إن الناسي على مذهب الامام الأعظم رضي الله تعالى عنه ليس بتارك للتسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says explicit-cause analogy may specify a general text by consensus.
rows.anchor: وأعترض بأن تخصيص العام الذي خص منه البعض جائز بالقياس المنصوص العلة وفاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection adds that deliberate omission need not mean the invocation is absent from the person's heart; the person might trust it and not feel a need to say it.
rows.anchor: ربما يكون لوثوقه بذلك وعدم افتقاره لذكره

rows.speaker: العلامة الثاني
rows.claim: He argues that the clause declaring it fisq refers to the act of omission, so forgetfulness is excluded because a forgetful person is neither sinful nor liable.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : فذهبوا إلى أن الناسي خارج بقوله تعالى : ( وانه لفسق ( إذ الضمير عائد إلى المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reports objections: emphatic fisq is not the apparent reading, conflicts with the parallel wording, and cannot apply to carrion, whose lack of invocation is not itself sinful.
rows.anchor: وأعترض ما ذكر بأن كون ذلك فسقا لا سيما على وجه التحقيق والتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation treats the slaughtered animal itself as fisq metaphorically, but it still must assume deliberate omission because forgetfulness is not sinful.
rows.anchor: أرجع الضمير إلى ( ما ) بمعنى الذبيحة وجعلها عين الفسق على سبيل المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Shafiʿi argument says a believer always has God's name in speech and heart, so only food dedicated to another deity is excluded.
rows.anchor: الأول ان التسمية على ذكر المؤمن وفي قلبه ما دام مؤمنا فلا يتحقق منه عدم الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another Shafiʿi argument says emphatic wording cannot condemn every disputed omission as fisq, since neither deliberate nor forgetful omission is unanimously sinful.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن قوله سبحانه : وإنه لفسق على وجه التحقيق والتأكيد لا يصح في حق أكل كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third Shafiʿi argument treats the fisq clause as circumstantial, restricting the prohibition to food dedicated to another deity; other food is permitted by contrary implication or general rules.
rows.anchor: والثالث أن هذه الجملة في موقع الحال إذ لا يحسن عطف الخبر على الانشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Objections say the circumstantial reading wrongly excludes carrion despite the occasion of revelation and clashes with the emphatic إن and lām, which suit an asserted independent clause rather than a conditional state.
rows.anchor: واعترض بانه يقتضي أن لا يتناول النهي أكل الميتة مع أنه سبب النزول

rows.speaker: العلامة
rows.claim: He answers that carrion is included through the following clause about satanic prompting; emphasis is fitting if fisq means dedication to another, which the polytheists deny.
rows.anchor: وأجاب العلامة عن الثاني بانه لما كان المراد بالفسق ههنا الاهلال لغير الله تعالى كان التأكيد مناسبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the verse as referring to carrion because the argument with the polytheists, described next, concerned that issue.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من تأول الآية بالميتة لأن الجدال فيها كما ستعلم قريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi considers the pronoun to refer most plausibly to the eating prohibited by ولا تأكلوا.
rows.anchor: واستظهر رجوع الضمير إلى الأكل الذي دل عليه ولا تأكلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general wording covers food dedicated to another, deliberate or forgetful omission, and carrion because carrion occasioned the revelation; al-Alusi says forgetfulness must be exempted by the report.
rows.anchor: الم يذكر اسم الله عليه عام لما أهل به لغير الله تعالى ولمتروك التسمية عمدا أو سهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An argument says general wording revealed for a particular cause is especially strong for that cause but weaker for other cases, reducing how much contrary evidence is needed.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد بأن العام الوارد على سبب خاص وإن قوى تناوله لسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument continues that the wording is explicit for the occasion but only apparent for other cases; al-Alusi says this ignores his preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: حتى ينتهض الظاهر فيه نصا إلا أنه ضعيف التناول لما عداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the foregoing argument fails for anyone who has understood the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى ما فيه لمن أحاط خبرا بما ذكره العلامة قبل

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Many Hanafi authorities say al-Shafiʿi conflicts with consensus: earlier jurists agreed that deliberate omission is forbidden, while they differed only about forgetful omission.
rows.anchor: وذكر كثير من أصحابنا أن قول الشافعي عليه الرحمة مخالف للأجماع

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar forbids eating an animal whose invocation was omitted forgetfully.
rows.anchor: فمذهب ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه يحرم ومذهب

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas permit eating an animal whose invocation was omitted forgetfully.
rows.anchor: ومذهب على كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباى رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه يحل

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف والمشايخ
rows.claim: They hold that deliberate omission leaves no room for legal reasoning; a judge's ruling permitting sale would be invalid as contrary to consensus.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يوسف والمشايخ رحمهم الله تعالى : إن متروك التسمية عامدا لا يسع فيه الاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent scope includes forgetful omission, but the law treats the forgetful person as one who remembered to relieve hardship because people often forget.
rows.anchor: وأن ظاهر الآية يقتضي شمولها لمتروك التسمية نسيانا إلأ أن الشرع جعل الناسي ذاكرا

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: A Shafiʿi objection compares the invocation to ritual purity: if it were a condition of lawful slaughter, forgetfulness should not excuse its omission.
rows.anchor: وقول بعض الشافعية عليهم الرحمة : إن التسمية لو كانت شرطا للحل لما سقط بعذر النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says that analogy wrongly equates deliberate and forgetful acts; equivalence applies when the forgetful person has a reminder, as in prayer, not where no reminder exists, as with fasting.
rows.anchor: مفض إلى التسوية بين العمد والنسيان وهي معهودة فيما إذا كان على الناسي هيئة مذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the change in the animal at death is not a reminder that would prompt the slaughterer to remember the invocation.
rows.anchor: وهنا إن لم تكن هيئة توجب النسيان وهي ما يحصل للذبائح عند زهوق روح حيوان من تغير الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi considers the issue open to juristic reasoning and consensus unproved; if consensus existed, al-Shafiʿi would not have violated it.
rows.anchor: والحق عندي أن المسئلة اجتهادية وثبوت الاجماع غير مسلم ولو كان ما كان خرقه الامام الشافعي

rows.speaker: الاصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Isfahani accuses al-Shafiʿi of violating seven Quranic verses; al-Alusi condemns this as an insult born of failing to appreciate the imam's learning and precision.
rows.anchor: وقول الاصفهاني كما في المستصفي أفحش الشافعي حيث خالف سبع آيات من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi calls the accusation an insult to this Qurashi imam, arising from failure to recognize his merit, broad learning, and subtle reasoning.
rows.anchor: من الفحش في حق هذا الامام القرشي ومثاره عدم الوقوف على فضله وسعة علمه ودقة نظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven verses cited include three in al-Anʿam, three in al-Hajj, and one in al-Maʾida.
rows.anchor: ثلاث منها في سورة الأنعام الاولى ( فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه ) والثانية

rows.speaker: عطاء وطاوس
rows.claim: Ataa and Tawus use the apparent wording to forbid food without invocation whether it is an animal or otherwise; the occasion of revelation weighs against this reading.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء وطاوس انهما استدلا بظاهرها على أن متروك التسمية حيوانا كان أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils are Iblis and his troops, whispering to their allies among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وإن الشياطين ( أي إبليس وجنوده ( ليوحون ( أي يوسوسون ( إلى أوليائهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the devils alternatively as rebellious Magians, who transmitted their argument to Quraysh through their allies.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وقيل : المراد بالشياطين مردة المجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urge debate through satanic whispering or the Magians' false arguments; obeying them means making forbidden things lawful.
rows.anchor: ليجادلوكم ( أي بالوساوس الشيطانية أو بما نقل من أباطيل المجوس ( وإن أطعتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who turns from obedience to God toward another, makes the forbidden lawful, and follows that other in religion has made that other a partner, preferring it to God.
rows.anchor: ضرورة أن من ترك طاعة الله تعالى إلى طاعة غيره واستحل الحرام واتبهة في دينه فقد أشركه

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Kaʿbi says the verse shows that faith names all acts of obedience, although its lexical meaning is assent.
rows.anchor: نقل الامام عن الكعبي أنه قال : الآية حجة على أن الايمان اسم لجميع الطاعات

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: By analogy, he says shirk names every act of disobedience, although the word literally refers to believing in a partner for God.
rows.anchor: كما جعل تعالى الشرك اسما لكل ما كان مخالفة لله عز وجل وإن كان في اللغة مختصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says shirk here could mean believing that God has a partner in legislation, so the term still refers only to belief.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يكون المراد من الشرك ههنا اعتقاد أن لله تعالى شريكا في الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says calling this obedience shirk is apparently an emphatic exaggeration, of which there are many parallels.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التعبير عن هذه الاطاعة بالشرك من باب التغليظ ونظأئره كثيرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan and others parse the wording as an oath: an omitted lām introduces the oath, the oath answer is إنكم لمشركون, and that answer also replaces the omitted conditional answer.
rows.anchor: والكلام هنا كما قال أبو حيان وغيره على تقدير القسم وحذف لام التوطئة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa and others instead make the stated clause the conditional answer without an oath, allowing omission of its fāʾ after a past-tense condition.
rows.anchor: وجعل أبو البقاء وتبعه بعضهم المذكور جواب الشرط ولا قسم وادعى أن حذف الفاء منه حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says Arabic grammarians require fāʾ before a nominal conditional answer and permit omission only in poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأن هذا لم يوجد في كتب العربية بل اتفق الكل على وجوب الفاء في الجملة الاسمية

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad allows omission of the fāʾ in ordinary prose, as al-Muradi mentions in his commentary on al-Tashil.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن المبرد أجاز ذلك في الاختيار كما ذكره المرادي في شرح التسهيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to state his true religion, which rival factions claim but have wholly abandoned; إنني emphasizes the statement's importance, and lordship is invoked with possessive address.
rows.anchor: أمر له صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يبين ما هو عليه من الدين الحق الذي يدعي المفرقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to tell the factions or all people that his Lord guided him by revelation and by signs in the horizons and souls to a path leading to truth.
rows.anchor: أي قل يا محمد لهؤلاء المفرقين أو للناس كافة : ارشدني ربي بالوحي وبما نصب في الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دينا may be appositive to the grammatical position of إلى صراط, as in 48:2; alternatively it may be the object of an implied verb or a second object of هداني.
rows.anchor: بدل من محل ( إلى صراط ) إد المعنى فهداني صراطا نظير قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قيما may be an intensive verbal noun used adjectivally or mean possessing stability; its expected form is قوما, while many readers use قيما as a derived form of قام.
rows.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( قيما ( مصدرا كالصغر والكبر نعت به مبالغة وجوز أن يكون التقدير ذا قيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say qayyim is stronger in its form while mustaqim is stronger in combined root and form; another argues mustaqim is stronger because its prefix expresses a demand for uprightness.
rows.anchor: وهو على ما قيل أبلغ من المستقيم باعتبار الهيئة والمستقيم أبلغ منه باعتبار مجموع المادة والهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many see no essential difference: both mean stable and ordering worldly and afterlife affairs; another view distinguishes the upright from the crooked and defines qayyim as enduring and unabrogated.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بين القيم والمستقيم في أصل المعنى عند الكثير وفسروا القيم بالثابت المقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملة إبراهيم is either appositional clarification of religion, despite differing definiteness, or an object under an implied verb meaning I mean.
rows.anchor: ملة إبراهيم نصب بتقدير أعني أو عطف بيان لدينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حنيفا means turned away from false religions or devoted sincerely to God; it is a circumstantial qualifier of Ibrahim, or an object of an implied verb.
rows.anchor: حنيفا ( أي مائلا عن الأديان الباطلة أو مخلصا لله تعالى في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may be a parenthetical confirming the Prophet's innocence of false beliefs or coordinate with the preceding statement; it rebuts Meccans, Jews, and Christians who each claim Abraham's way while attributing a son to God.
rows.anchor: ( اعتراض مقرر لنزاهته عليه الصلاة والسلام عما عليه المبطلون وقيل : عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قال begins a fresh statement like similar passages. فاء sequences Satan's statement after the respite; باء may mark an oath or cause, and ما is then a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الفاء لترتيب مضمون الجملة التي بعد على الانظار والباء أما للقسم أو للسببية وما على التقديرين مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed causal reading attaches the prepositional phrase to what follows, but this is rejected because the phrase has precedence and cannot be governed backward; reading ما as a question is also weak.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن لها الصدر على الصحيح فلا يعمل ما بعدها فيما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ighwa means creating error; the root first means corruption, also ignorance from false belief, failure, and metaphorical punishment as a consequence.
rows.anchor: والاغواء خلق الغي وأصل الغي الفساد ومنه غوي الفصيل وغوى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the phrase means God created misguidance in Satan; Sunnis accept this, supported by the universal statement that God creates everything.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما ونسبة الاغواء بهذا المعنى إلى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila reject attributing misguidance to God: they call Satan's statement no proof, or construe the verb as labeling someone astray or causing error by commanding prostration.
rows.anchor: والمعتزلة يأبون نسبة مثل ذلك اليه سبحانه وقالوا في هذا تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others interpret ghayy as failure, loss of mercy, or destruction through God's curse and expulsion; al-Alusi says this reflects their refusal to accept God as creator of all things.
rows.anchor: إن الغي هنا بمعنى الخيبة أي بما خيبته من رحمتك أو الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot mean enticing someone toward error or commanding it, which is the sense intended in Satan's threat to lead people astray.
rows.anchor: نعم الاغواء بمعنى الترغيب بما فيه الغواية والامر به كما هو مراد اللعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase is an oath, Satan swears by an attribute of divine action, though jurists do not apply legal-oath rulings to such an oath.
rows.anchor: ثم إن كانت الباء للقسم يكون المقسم به صفة من صفات الافعال وهو مما يقسم به في العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perhaps Satan swore by both misguidance and might, with the Quran mentioning one oath at each point; on the causal reading, he swears by God's might because God misled him for their sake.
rows.anchor: ولعل القسم وقع من اللعين بهما جميعا فكى تارة قسمه باحدهما وأخرى بالآخر وان كانت سببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan means Adam and his descendants by them, and promises to lie in wait on their path as a highway robber waits for travelers.
rows.anchor: لاقعدن لهم ( أي لآدم عليه السلام وذريته ترصدا بهم كما يقعد القطاع للسابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the path leading to Paradise, the truth that pleases God.
rows.anchor: الموصل إلى الجنة وهو الحق الذي فيه رضاك

rows.speaker: سبرة بن الفاكه
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan waits at the paths to Islam, migration, and jihad, urging people to abandon each; those who disobey him and persevere are promised Paradise.
rows.anchor: أخرج أحمد والنسائي وابن حبان والطبراني والبيهقي في شعب الايمان عن سبة بن الفاكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report lists these paths to emphasize their great rank in this context, not to limit Satan's temptations to them.
rows.anchor: ولعل الاقتصار منه صلى الله عليه وسلم على هذه المذكورات للاعتناء بشأنها والتنبيه على عظم قدرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: They and others interpret the straight path as the road to Mecca; al-Alusi calls this a figure of speech or representation.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنهما وغيرهما من تفسير الصراط المستقيم بطريق مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative الصراط can be the object by construing اقعدن as persist, can omit على, or can be a locative adverbial, a rare use with a specific place.
rows.anchor: ونصب الصراط اما على أنه مفعول به بتضمين ( أقعدن ) معنى الزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited verse of poetry illustrates the locative construction with a definite place noun.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك في المشهور قوله : لدن بهز الكف يعسل متنه فيه كما عسل الطريق الثعلب
